assets.name: T-catalogue.png
assets.shows: 1080x1920 capture of catalogue/ASSET-CATALOG.html as Chrome renders it: the six script beats as cards, then the asset table with thumbnails, file specs, what each file is and shows, where it earns its place, what it binds to, its tags and its beat. Taken before this capture and the tracks capture were added to the folder, which is the catalogue the trailer is talking about.

assets.name: T-notebook.png
assets.role: ★ This trailer's own NOTEBOOK.md, in a dark editor

assets.name: T-finalcut-editor.mov
assets.role: ★ The Paganini timeline inside Final Cut Pro (the creator's screen recording)
assets.shows: 6.07 s, 1918x1200, 30 fps, silent. The whole Final Cut Pro window: the viewer top centre playing the tutorial with a yellow caption on it, the timeline across the bottom with the primary storyline, connected title clips above it and the playhead moving right. Window 16.0-22.0 s of the creator's 93 s recording of the .fcpxml import.
assets.use: B5, under 'a real timeline for Final Cut Pro'. Landscape in a portrait reel: letterboxed, which is fine for four seconds.
assets.binds_to: a `<video clip of a REAL timeline imported into Final Cut Pro ...>` type component

assets.name: T-side-by-side.mov
assets.role: ★ Final Cut Pro | DaVinci Resolve, the same storyboard side by side
assets.shows: 8.0 s, 2160x1920, 30 fps, silent. Two 1080x1920 renders side by side, Final Cut Pro left, DaVinci Resolve right. The caption 'same interval, smaller space' lands at ~0.8 s on both, the cut to the fingerboard close-up at ~2.0 s on both, 'why not octaves?' at ~3.9 s on both. Window 33.4-41.4 s of the two-panel comparison movie of the current build.
assets.use: B5, under 'Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve'; the picture that says 'two editors, one storyboard'.
assets.binds_to: a `<video clip of the same storyboard rendered by Final Cut Pro and by DaVinci Resolve side by side>` type component

assets.name: T-tracks.mov
assets.role: ★ This trailer's own REEL-TRACKS.html, the playhead moving
assets.shows: 7.17 s, 1920x1080, 30 fps, silent. The tracks page of this very reel, captured by Chrome through its #t= deep link at 15 captures per second: the playhead crosses the hook and the first four-files beat (reel time 0-7.17 s), the preview pane composites the frame at the playhead, the caption block 'it shows its work' sits on its anchor word in the text lane. Landscape; the storyboard letterboxes it.
assets.use: B4, under 'Every picture is pinned to a word, not a timestamp'. The beat the trailer exists for.
assets.binds_to: a `<video clip of REAL's own REEL-TRACKS.html for this trailer, the playhead moving ...>` type component

assets.name: T-tutorial-render.mov
assets.role: ★ The finished tutorial as Final Cut Pro rendered it (hook)
assets.shows: 5.8 s, 1080x1920, 30 fps, WITH the tutorial's own narration (the violinist speaking; keep it silent under the trailer's voice). Opens on the score-excerpt still over the violinist; the caption 'fingered octaves, Paganini 23' lands at ~0.8 s and holds to ~2.6 s; the cut to the fingerboard close-up at ~2.9 s; the close-up to the end. Window 18.8-24.6 s of the creator's Final Cut export of the current build.
assets.use: B1, the hook: 'REAL edits yours' over the creator's own footage already edited, a caption landing, then a cut.
assets.binds_to: a `<video clip of the finished Paganini tutorial as rendered by Final Cut Pro ...>` type component
